meta.title: EcoTrace – Trace emissions back to source documents
meta.description: An open-source platform for document intake, review, approvals and traceable Scope 1 and 2 emissions.
hero.title: Every emission figure has a source document.
hero.body: Read invoices, review data, approve activities and calculate Scope 1 and 2 emissions. One open-source core serves multiple companies, with each workflow defined by configuration.
hero.note: Runs on-premise with Docker Compose. AI is optional; electronic invoice XML is parsed directly.
invoice.title: Electricity bill
invoice.table: Fields from the sample electricity bill
invoice.review: The rule-based extractor returns 60% confidence, below Company A's 80% threshold: human review is required.
invoice.after: Sample emissions after review and approval
invoice.factor: 188,800 kWh × 0.681 kgCO₂e/kWh. The demo factor is provisional and must be replaced with an official factor before reporting.
invoice.source: View the fictional demo document in the repository
problem.label: The problem
problem.title: Keep the path from each figure to its source.
problem.intake.title: Scattered documents
problem.intake.body: PDFs, photos and XML enter one pipeline: scan for malware, store the original and extract according to company configuration.
problem.review.title: Retyping and corrections
problem.review.body: Uncertain fields are flagged. Each correction preserves the previous value, new value and reviewer before approval.
problem.evidence.title: Missing evidence
problem.evidence.body: Each result retains its document, approver and factor version. Closed periods are sealed so changes can be detected.
how.label: How it works
how.title: Six steps from a document to a reporting period.
step.1.title: Upload a document
step.1.body: Authenticate the company, scan for malware and store the original in the company's bucket.
step.2.title: Read and classify
step.2.body: Parse XML directly; PDFs and photos use optional AI or the rule-based fallback.
step.3.title: Review the data
step.3.body: A reviewer corrects fields below the confidence threshold; every correction is recorded.
step.4.title: Follow the approval workflow
step.4.body: Each company's BPMN process defines the responsible roles and number of approval steps.
step.5.title: Calculate and trace
step.5.body: Activity quantity multiplied by a factor produces emissions. The result retains its source and factor version.
step.6.title: Close and seal the period
step.6.body: Record a verifiable seal in Trillian, check for changes and export Excel or CSV reports.
trace.label: Traceability
trace.title: One figure, with the evidence needed to check it.
roles.label: Roles
roles.title: Clear responsibilities for each person.
roles.accountant.work: Upload, compare with the original and correct the data.
roles.approver.work: Approve or reject items in the task inbox.
roles.approver.evidence: Decision maker and each BPMN step.
roles.inventory.work: Track Scope 1 and 2, close periods and export figures.
roles.inventory.evidence: Activity quantity, factor and sealed reporting period.
roles.reviewer.work: Follow the lineage and verify period seals.
architecture.label: Architecture
architecture.title: Three tiers, configured for each company.
architecture.apps: Enabled or disabled per company. Both use reviewed documents and approval workflows.
architecture.capabilities: Services communicate through the API gateway and events. The interface supports Vietnamese and English.
architecture.core: One shared Keycloak realm with tenant_id; services use RLS, while Hasura applies per-company permissions.
architecture.planned: OpenBao, Kestra, monitoring, meter reconciliation and Kubernetes remain planned. Example config packs live in tenants/; dxctl onboards companies.
faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Before you try it.
faq.certification.a: No. It prepares figures and evidence for an independent verifier. Scope 3 and carbon credit trading are outside the project's scope.
faq.ai.q: Are documents sent to an external AI service?
faq.ai.a: Only when AI is enabled for the deployment. XML is parsed locally; without an API key, the fallback reads PDFs with a text layer and cannot read images. Demos use fictional documents.
faq.review.q: What happens to incorrect data or duplicate uploads?
faq.review.a: A reviewer corrects data before approval; history retains both old and new values. Matching file content is detected to avoid processing it twice.
faq.tenants.q: Does onboarding a company require code changes?
faq.tenants.a: No. A config pack defines users, documents, emission sources and BPMN workflows. dxctl validates and applies it; automated checks cover isolation and onboarding.
run.label: Run locally
run.title: Clone, configure, start.
run.requirements: Linux or WSL 2, Docker Compose, git, make, curl and jq. 16 GB RAM is recommended; the first run needs internet access to pull images.
run.secrets: Replace the change-me values in .env before sharing the demo host.
run.open: Open http://localhost:9080 and log in with the demo account described in the guide.
